title: Glenn T
content: I was around 12 years old. We were on a family holiday, staying in a weathered, old caravan park by the coast. I was the kind of place where the salty wind never really stops blowing and everything smells faintly of seaweed and sunscreen. One afternoon, I borrowed a friend’s surfboard that was dinged and faded with peeling wax. I wasn’t much of a surfer, but the waves looked inviting. Curiosity got the better of me. I paddled out alone. The beach was eerily quiet with the distant chatter of seagulls and the rhythmic crash of water on sand. I’d only been in the water for maybe ten minutes when I caught a small, lazy wave while lying flat on my stomach. I let the wave carry me toward shore. The wave deposited me gently onto the wet sand. I lay there for a moment, catching my breath and feeling the sun on my back. A rogue wave came from nowhere. The wave was, taller and faster than the rest. It slammed into me before I could react. I got pulled underwater several times. All I could see was a blur of green water and foam. At first, I panicked, but then the fear melted away. Everything around me grew strangely quiet. Suddenly, I wasn’t in the ocean anymore. I was somewhere else, inside a distant memory I had forgotten. It felt like the memory belonged to someone else, but it was mine. I could move through the memories. It was as if I could turn through moments, like pages in an old book. Each memory was vivid and alive. I drifted between scenes from a few years earlier; fragments of life I hadn’t thought about in forever. Yet, I wasn’t watching them because I was in them. Time seemed to stretch. I could stay in any memory as long as I wanted. Then, abruptly, the vision shattered. I was back on the beach, coughing and vomiting seawater into the sand. The taste of salt burned my throat. Dizzy, I scrambled to my feet, dazed and shivering. What haunted me wasn’t the wave. It was the strange journey I’d taken. It didn’t feel like a dream. It felt real. I didn’t tell anyone. I just hurried back to the caravan park, heart pounding, unsure of what had just happened and why.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: No, Drowning, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, -
elements.Please compare your hearing during the e: I don't think I heard any sound
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: Memories are the best way to describe it
elements.Did scenes from your past come back to y: I was in memories. A cubby house at a friend's house was one of the memories I remember clearly.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, -
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was probably not real, Felt like a dream, I guess.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was probably real, It felt like the dying process was starting up, but didn't get far in.
